newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar recovers ground at the close.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar recovers ground at the close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed on Tuesday at US$0.6890/00 after recovering some of the ground it lost in the immediate aftermath of better-than- expected CPI data and a weaker Australian dollar.
The kiwi closed down 13 basis points at 68.59 on the Trade Weighted Index.
"It has traded in a pretty narrow range of 0.6875-6913 and since the CPI data 0.6895 has been the high and 0.6975 the low," a Wellington-based chief dealer said.
The CPI for the March quarter came in at a fall of 0.3 percent against expectations of a rise of 0.1 percent.

"There has been pretty strong exporter buying -- they have been hanging out for these levels for a while. It may now hang around here a little longer and then go lower I think," the chief dealer said.
He said offshore interest was dominated by sellers and this could see the kiwi lower overnight to a base of about 0.6860.
"Based on where conditions are at the moment monetary conditions are reasonably too firm and I expect the RBNZ to move. The first part of that could be a comment tomorrow," he said.
An Auckland-based dealer said there had been an overall easing of monetary conditions on the day but there was good exporter and short covering demand underpinning the currency.
"Overall I think the market is looking to sell rallies either through a spike in the kiwi or a rally in the TWI," he said.
He said he, too, expected a comment from the RBNZ if the currency didn't ease overnight. "Conditions don't need to be as tight, as evidenced by the data today."
